### Problem: Filling bookcase shelves {#sec-od-p5-shelf}

::: {.p-statement}
Books are pairs $[\mathrm{thickness}, \mathrm{height}]$ and must stay in the given order. A shelf is at most `shelfWidth` thick and as tall as its tallest book. Return the minimum total height of the bookcase. Here $1 \le n \le 1000$, each thickness is at least 1 and at most the width, and heights are at most 1000.

Source: [LC 1105 · Filling Bookcase Shelves](https://leetcode.com/problems/filling-bookcase-shelves/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The shelves are a cut of the sequence into consecutive blocks. Filling every shelf as full as it will go scores 8 on the sample; the optimum is 6, because leaving the first short book alone lets the two tall books share a shelf. The last shelf of an optimal placement of the first $i$ books is some segment $[j, i)$ whose thickness is at most the width, and that shelf costs its maximum height.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[i]$ = minimum height for the first $i$ books.
- **Transition.** $dp[i] = \min (dp[j] + \max(h_j, \ldots, h_{i-1}))$ over every $j$ whose books $j..i-1$ fit on one shelf.
- **Inner loop.** $j$ walks from $i-1$ down. Each step adds one book on the left, so width and height update in $O(1)$. The first width that exceeds the limit ends the loop: every smaller $j$ is wider still.
- **Base.** $dp[0] = 0$. **Answer.** $dp[n]$.
:::

::: {#fig-od-shelf}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
books = [[1, 1], [2, 3], [2, 3], [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 2]]
width = 4
n = len(books)
dp = [10**9] * (n + 1)
dp[0] = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    thick = height = 0
    for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
        thick += books[j][0]
        if thick > width:
            break
        height = max(height, books[j][1])
        dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[j] + height)
assert dp[-1] == 6 and dp == [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6]
def draw(ax, p):
    V.array(ax, p, dp, label="dp", colors={0: "amber", 1: "green", 3: "green", 7: "indigo"})
V.show(draw)
```

Sample, width 4. The green cells are the shelf breaks of one optimum: book 0 alone (height 1), books 1–2 (height 3), books 3–6 (height 2). Total 6.

:::

::: {.callout-important title="Why a window of the width is legal"}
A shelf holds at most $W$ books, because every thickness is at least 1. So $dp[i]$ reads only $dp[j]$ for $j \ge i-W$. Cells older than that are dead, and a ring of length $\min(n, W)+1$ keeps exactly the live window. The residues $i, i-1, \ldots, i-W$ are distinct modulo $\min(n, W)+1$, so a read of $dp[j]$ does not pick up a newer value. With $n, W \le 1000$ the ring saves nothing you can feel; the point is how far back a partition looks.

The early `break` is the same fact in the other direction. Width only grows as $j$ moves left, so the first infeasible shelf proves every longer shelf infeasible. `continue` would be correct and slower. Moving $j$ from 0 upward shrinks the shelf, the running maximum cannot be undone, and the height is recomputed from scratch: $O(n^3)$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`solve(i)` tries every legal last shelf of the first `i` books and adds that shelf's height to `solve(j)`. `solve(0) = 0`. With a wide shelf every cut is legal and there are $2^{n-1}$ of them.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("shelf", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def shelf_rec(books, width):
    def solve(i):
        if i == 0:
            return 0
        best, thick, height = 10**9, 0, 0
        for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
            thick += books[j][0]
            if thick > width:
                break
            height = max(height, books[j][1])
            best = min(best, solve(j) + height)
        return best
    return solve(len(books))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int shelfRec(int i, const vector<vector<int>>& books, int width) {
    if (i == 0) return 0;
    int best = 1e9, thick = 0, height = 0;
    for (int j = i - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
        thick += books[j][0];
        if (thick > width) break;
        height = max(height, books[j][1]);
        best = min(best, shelfRec(j, books, width) + height);
    }
    return best;
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
`solve(i)` depends only on how many books are already placed. Cache it. The inner loop is the same walk toward the left, with the same break.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("shelf", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "4"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def shelf_memo(books, width):
    memo = [-1] * (len(books) + 1)

    def solve(i):
        if i == 0:
            return 0
        if memo[i] < 0:
            best, thick, height = 10**9, 0, 0
            for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
                thick += books[j][0]
                if thick > width:
                    break
                height = max(height, books[j][1])
                best = min(best, solve(j) + height)
            memo[i] = best
        return memo[i]

    return solve(len(books))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int shelfMemo(int i, const vector<vector<int>>& books, int width, vector<int>& memo) {
    if (i == 0) return 0;
    if (memo[i] >= 0) return memo[i];
    int best = 1e9, thick = 0, height = 0;
    for (int j = i - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
        thick += books[j][0];
        if (thick > width) break;
        height = max(height, books[j][1]);
        best = min(best, shelfMemo(j, books, width, memo) + height);
    }
    return memo[i] = best;
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
`dp[i]` is `solve(i)` written from the left. `dp[0] = 0` is the empty bookcase. The last shelf grows by one book per inner step; test the width before the height is allowed to update the answer. An infeasible shelf must not be scored once and then rejected.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("shelf", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def shelf_table(books, width):
    n = len(books)
    dp = [10**9] * (n + 1)
    dp[0] = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        thick = height = 0
        for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
            thick += books[j][0]
            if thick > width:
                break
            height = max(height, books[j][1])
            dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[j] + height)
    return dp[n]
```

##### C++

```cpp
int shelfTable(const vector<vector<int>>& books, int width) {
    int n = (int)books.size();
    vector<int> dp(n + 1, 1e9);
    dp[0] = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        int thick = 0, height = 0;
        for (int j = i - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
            thick += books[j][0];
            if (thick > width) break;
            height = max(height, books[j][1]);
            dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[j] + height);
        }
    }
    return dp[n];
}
```
:::

#### Rolling

::: {.form-next}
Keep `min(n, width) + 1` cells. `ring[i % R]` is `dp[i]`. The inner loop only reads starts inside the last `width` books, and those residues are still the values from this layer. The sample still returns 6.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("shelf", "roll")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def shelf_roll(books, width):
    n = len(books)
    ring_n = min(n, width) + 1
    ring = [0] * ring_n
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        best, thick, height = 10**9, 0, 0
        for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
            thick += books[j][0]
            if thick > width:
                break
            height = max(height, books[j][1])
            best = min(best, ring[j % ring_n] + height)
        ring[i % ring_n] = best
    return ring[n % ring_n]

BOOKS = [[1, 1], [2, 3], [2, 3], [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 2]]
assert shelf_table(BOOKS, 4) == 6
assert shelf_roll([[1, 3], [2, 4], [3, 2]], 6) == 4
assert shelf_table([[1, 1], [1, 10], [1, 10]], 2) == 11
for books, w in ((BOOKS, 4), ([[1, 3], [2, 4], [3, 2]], 6), ([[1, 1], [1, 10], [1, 10]], 2)):
    assert shelf_rec(books, w) == shelf_memo(books, w) == shelf_table(books, w) == shelf_roll(books, w)
random.seed(4)
for _ in range(20):
    w = random.randint(1, 4)
    books = [[random.randint(1, w), random.randint(1, 5)] for _ in range(random.randint(1, 6))]
    assert shelf_rec(books, w) == shelf_table(books, w) == shelf_roll(books, w)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int shelfRoll(const vector<vector<int>>& books, int width) {
    int n = (int)books.size();
    int R = min(n, width) + 1;
    vector<int> ring(R);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        int best = 1e9, thick = 0, height = 0;
        for (int j = i - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
            thick += books[j][0];
            if (thick > width) break;
            height = max(height, books[j][1]);
            best = min(best, ring[j % R] + height);
        }
        ring[i % R] = best;
    }
    return ring[n % R];
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** up to $2^{n-1}$. **Memo**, the **table**, and the **ring** are $O(n \cdot \min(n, W))$ time. The table uses $O(n)$ memory; the ring uses $O(\min(n, W))$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- One book returns its height. A shelf of width equal to that thickness is legal.
- $[[1,1],[1,10],[1,10]]$ with width 2 is 11, not the greedy 20. The first book sits alone.
- Books of thickness $W$ force one book per shelf. The order is part of the input: do not sort.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Updating the answer before the width test. The infeasible shelf is then scored once.
- Walking $j$ from the left. The running maximum cannot be undone, and the inner loop becomes $O(n)$.
- Sorting the books by height. The statement fixes the order; sorting solves a different problem.
:::

**Variants.** [LC 1043 · Partition Array for Maximum Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/partition-array-for-maximum-sum/){difficulty="Medium"} drops the width and scores a block of length at most $k$ as $k$ times its maximum. [LC 410 · Split Array Largest Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/split-array-largest-sum/){difficulty="Hard"} uses exactly $k$ blocks and the cost of a cut is the largest block sum, not a total.
